title: Inner, left and cocartesian fibrations of simplicial sets
statement:
Use the simplicial sets of [def-weil-pbc-simplicial-set] and the standard simplices, horns, quasicategories and simplicial maps of [def-cbc-enhanced-diagrams-cones]. For a simplicial map $p:E\to B$, to have the right lifting property for an inclusion $K\subseteq L$ means that every pair $u:K\to E$, $v:L\to B$ with $pu=v|_K$ admits $w:L\to E$ with $w|_K=u$ and $pw=v$. An inner fibration has this property for $\Lambda_i^n\subseteq\Delta^n$, $n\geq2$, $0<i<n$. A left fibration has it for $n\geq1$, $0\leq i<n$; a right fibration has it for $n\geq1$, $0<i\leq n$.

For an inner fibration $p$, an edge $e:\Delta^1\to E$ is $p$-cocartesian if, for every $n\geq2$, every lifting problem for $\Lambda_0^n\subseteq\Delta^n$ whose upper map restricts to $e$ on the ordered edge $\{0,1\}$ has a filler over $B$. It is $p$-cartesian if the corresponding condition holds for $\Lambda_n^n$ and the ordered edge $\{n-1,n\}$. For quasicategories $E,B$, a cocartesian fibration is an inner fibration such that for each vertex $x\in E$ and edge $\alpha:p(x)\to b$ in $B$, there is a $p$-cocartesian edge with source $x$ lying over $\alpha$. A cartesian fibration instead requires a $p$-cartesian lift with target $y$ for every edge $b\to p(y)$. A fiber over $b$ is the degreewise pullback $E\times_B\{b\}$. A functor over the same base preserves cocartesian (respectively cartesian) edges if it takes every such edge to an edge of the same kind.
